meta.titre: Bouncer: run several notch apps on one MacBook
meta.description: Vibe Island, boringNotch and NotchNook in the same notch, without drawing over each other. Bouncer shows one, and a two-finger swipe moves to the next. Free, open source, macOS 14+.
meta.ogAlt: A MacBook notch showing a single app, with the title “All your notch apps. One on screen.”

chrome.piedLigne: Bouncer, a utility for macOS 14 and later. MIT licence.

apercu.indice: Swipe here with two fingers, or press <kbd>⌃⌥⌘B</kbd>
apercu.annonceRelance: Relaunching {app}. The current app stays until the new one is on screen.

heros.surtitre: For notched MacBooks running two notch apps or more
heros.pourQui: Vibe Island tracks your agents, boringNotch your music, NotchNook your files, and they all draw in the same spot under the notch. Bouncer shows one and puts the others aside. A two-finger swipe on the notch moves to the next.
heros.voirCompatibles: Does it work with my apps? ›
heros.mentions: <lien>Source code on GitHub</lien> · macOS 14 or later · no account
heros.surMac: Bouncer runs on your Mac. Open this page on your MacBook.

probleme.chapo: Vibe Island, boringNotch, NotchNook, Notchy: each one draws its own pill under your notch. Open two and they land on the same rectangle, one over the other.
probleme.corps: macOS has no idea which one should be in front. <fort>The only way out it gives you is to quit one app to see the other</fort>, then reopen it when you need it back. Bouncer does that rotation for you with one gesture, and only removes the current app once the next one is on screen.
probleme.sans: Without Bouncer: both apps draw into the same rectangle
probleme.avec: With Bouncer: one app on screen, the others wait their turn
probleme.mainCorps: Quit the app, reopen the other one from Spotlight, wait for it to load. Then do it all again the other way.
probleme.avecCorps: One swipe. The switch takes ≈ 50 ms when the app can be hidden, ≈ 1 s when it has to be relaunched.

commandes.chapo: Take whichever is closest to hand. They all move one step through the cycle, and the cycle loops.
commandes.swipeCorps: Pointer over the notch app, two fingers sideways on the trackpad. Left or right makes no difference, the gesture moves one step.
commandes.flechesCorps: Bring the cursor near the camera housing and two arrows appear on either side. Click one. Away from the notch, Bouncer draws nothing.
commandes.raccourciCorps: Works from any app, full screen included. Without a trackpad, it is the one command that makes you neither aim at the notch nor open a menu.
commandes.menuCorps: No Dock icon, no window. ● is the app holding the notch, ○ one waiting, ◐ a switch in progress. Click a waiting app to bring it back.

moteur.chapo: Depending on the app, Bouncer hides it or relaunches it. It picks on its own, there’s nothing to set.

chiffre1.note: Vibe Island, Cyclop, gh-notch, NotchNook: 46 to 57 ms measured, faster than a blink. The app stays open and comes back where you left it.

chiffre3.libelle: for apps that won’t be hidden
chiffre3.note: boringNotch, Notchy and Mew Notch ignore the hide command, so Bouncer quits them when another app takes the notch and reopens them when you come back. In between, they show nothing.

moteur.friseCorps: Bouncer only removes the current app once the next one is on screen. If the next one won’t start, or takes more than five seconds, nothing moves. You never end up staring at an empty notch halfway through a switch.
moteur.friseLegende: Timeline of a relaunch: {arrive} starts, shows up at about two thirds of a second, then {part} closes.
moteur.refusCorps: No undocumented system tricks, the kind that break on a macOS update. An app that refuses to quit is never force-killed. It may have something to save, so Bouncer leaves it alone.
moteur.detectionCorps: Bouncer never touches it. It only deals with the small windows stuck to the notch. <lien>The full method, for the curious ›</lien>

compatibilite.pasPourVous: Not for you if you only run one notch app. With just one, there’s nothing for Bouncer to choose between.

installation.chapo: Free, open source, and about a minute to install.
installation.zipCorps: A .zip from the releases page. Unzip it and drag Bouncer into Applications.
installation.brewCorps: One line in the terminal. Bouncer lands in Applications and opens normally.
installation.gatekeeperQuestion: “macOS cannot verify that Bouncer is free of malware”
installation.gatekeeper1: You will see this on first launch of the downloaded app. Apple charges developers €99 a year for an identity it recognises on sight, and Bouncer doesn’t pay it. The block is about that missing identity. The app is neither damaged nor infected.
installation.gatekeeper2: To open it anyway, once: double-click Bouncer and let macOS refuse, then open System Settings, Privacy & Security, and click “Open Anyway”.
installation.gatekeeper3: Through Homebrew you never see this message, because the cask strips the quarantine attribute itself. That’s a Gatekeeper workaround we write ourselves, and it goes away the day Bouncer is notarised by Apple.
installation.accesCorps: To read the window list and hide your notch apps’ windows. Without it, Bouncer touches nothing. The code is public on <lien>GitHub</lien>.
installation.sortieCorps: Bouncer can send its crash reports to Sentry. That’s off by default, and nothing is sent until you turn it on in the Bouncer menu.
installation.desinstallerCorps: Drag Bouncer to the Bin, or run brew uninstall --zap bouncer if you installed it with Homebrew.
